newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia 96/97 summer crops look good-ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia 96/97 summer crops look good-ABARE.

text.p: Good early prospects for 1996/97 Australian summer crop plantings in the states of Queensland and New South Wales had been consolidated by well-spaced October and November rainfall, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said in its Australian Crop Report.

Sowings were well underway in central Queensland and early indications confirmed a forecast swing to sunflower plantings at the expense of sorghum sowings after falling cereal prices in recent months, it said.
Summer crop plantings in southern Queensland and northern New South Wales had been delayed by the late harvesting of large winter crops, it said.
In addition, the large plantings of winter crops in 1996/97 had reduced the area available to plant summer crops, particularly in Queensland, it said.

On individual summer crops, ABARE said sorghum production was expected to contract by a third to about one million tonnes in 1996/97. Total sorghum plantings were expected to contract by 28 percent to 472,000 hectares, it said.
Total sunflower plantings were forecast to more than double to 158,000 hectares in 1996/97, ABARE said.
Soybean plantings were expected to increase by 44 percent to 46,000 hectares in 1996/97, with most of the increased area in traditional cattle country, particularly coastal New South Wales, it said.
Rice growers had planted an unprecedented 165,000 hectares to rice in 1996/97, or 26,000 hectares more than in 1995/96, it said.

Cool spring weather and locusts had reduced yield potential slightly but, assuming normal seasonal conditions, production of rice in 1996/97 is forecast to reach a record 1.45 million tonnes, ABARE said.
This is up on ABARE's last Crop Report forecast, which set Ausrtralia's 1996/97 rice crop at 1.34 million tonnes.
Production in 1995/96 was 951,000 tonnes after being adversely affected by cool weather.
ABARE is also frecasting a record Australian cotton crop of 2.5 million 500 lb bales, or 571,000 tonnes, up from 420,000 tonnes in 1995/96. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
